items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: We got a drummer out of Chicago -- a beautiful drummer, a white dude named Guy Devereaux

ctx.x: We worked from 9 until daylight. And Jive was making all the money. We didn't question it, so long as he kept our habits up, you know. And had a roof over our head.

Well, I did that up until about 1950 -- that was about a year -- '49-50 was my hardest time, and the guy offered me a job with Billie Holiday -- a little club on the north side; a trio -- she had a piano player, Carl Drinkard, and yeah, I want to make it. We got a drummer out of Chicago -- a beautiful drummer, a white dude named Guy Devereaux -- he loved Ike Day and played just like him, and I don't know whether he thought he
thought he was supposed to play with sticks behind Billy, but he did ...
